reasoning: 3een has ee plus the possessive -o. Dayy'a has emphatic ض as D, shadda on ي and ق as a glottal stop; taa marbuta after ق is a. Idiomatic for stingy or small-minded.
A Ramallah speaker says itjawwaz, from جوز, not tzawwaj; the form given is the written-Arabic one. Read aloud it comes out tzawwaj with the first vowel dropped.
Young Ramallah slang, used after an adjective as a booster, 7ilu fashikh. The second vowel is a short front vowel, which the scheme writes i; some speakers say it as a bare cluster fashkh.
ma negates the b-imperfect verb; bibayyin has shadda on ي. 3aleek has ee. Typically a compliment, as in 'you don't look your age'.
ث becomes t in Ramallah, so ثقيل is respelled تِقِيل, and ق is a glottal stop: ti'iil.
ق glottalises: ta'diir. Besides appreciation and estimation it is the word for an academic grade classification.
Short i then a final cluster: jisr, plural jsuur. Also used of the Jordan crossing, il-jisr.
Two long oo vowels and a final -ya cluster: kooloombya. Country names like this are borrowed as they are.
ح is 7 and the short vowel before ي drops in Palestinian: naa7ye, taa marbuta as e. 'From one side / in one respect', usually paired with w min naa7ye taanye.
A denominal defective verb from farshaaye, past farsha, imperfect yifarshi, used of brushing teeth or hair. Low confidence because many Ramallah speakers instead say ghasal snaano.
ح is 7; both members take the article, and ب and م are moon letters so it stays il-. The shadda doubles ي: il-mayyit.
ق is a glottal stop and ط is T; in the construct the taa marbuta is pronounced t, so I respell it نُقْطَت. ض is D in Da3f.
Palestinian imperfect prefix ti- for the masculine addressee, emphatic ص as S. kheer has ee, not ii.
ث becomes t, so ثاني is respelled تَانِي. Besides the ordinal 'second' it very commonly means 'other / another'.
ح is 7 in both halves; the linking la- is written with a hyphen as a prefix. Idiomatic for doing something quietly behind the scenes.
Same word as the adjective for weight, respelled تِقِيل for Palestinian t and glottal ق. Of a person it means tiresome, heavy going, someone whose company drags.
Short i then the final -ya: dinya. In Ramallah id-dinya also stands for life in general and for the weather.
ع is 3 and the shadda doubles د: mu3addal. The standard word for a school or university average.
Emphatic ط as T with the shadda doubling ن: Tannash. Everyday Ramallah slang for deliberately ignoring someone.
ق is a glottal stop and the final hamza is not pronounced, so قرأ is respelled قَرَا: 'ara, imperfect bi'ra.
Palestinian participle mi7taaj with i in the prefix, ح as 7. 3amaliyye is the word used for a surgical operation, taa marbuta as e after ي.
ween 'where' has ee, not ii, and is the Palestinian form against MSA ayna. With ma kaan it generalises to 'wherever'.

Instrument noun with Palestinian i in the prefix, taa marbuta as e after س: miknase. The vowels vary between speakers, hence low confidence; the same word covers a vacuum cleaner, miknase kahrabaa'iyye.
Initial hamza is the bare vowel, final hamza is written ': intimaa'. It means belonging or affiliation; 'identity' proper is hawiyye.
Palestinian prefix yi-, with the feminine object -ha standing for 'your way'. bi- reduces to b before the cluster: bwijhak, to a man.
